# Synthetic comparison case — not a literature source

The following made-up studies test whether a review workflow respects battery evidence boundaries. They are not real papers and have no DOI.

| Field | Study A | Study B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chemistry | sodium-ion hard carbon | sodium-ion hard carbon |
| Configuration | hard carbon vs sodium-metal half cell, coin | hard-carbon cathode-paired full cell, pouch |
| Quoted result | 340 mAh per gram of hard-carbon active material, desodiation, cycle 2 | projected 150 Wh per kg of complete cell from a design model |
| Current | 20 mA per gram of active material | not supplied in fixture |
| Temperature | 25 °C | not supplied in fixture |
| Electrode loading | not supplied in fixture | 12 mg per square centimeter |
| Electrolyte amount | not supplied in fixture | not supplied in fixture |
| Sodium inventory or presodiation | sodium-metal counter electrode | presodiation assumed in model, amount not supplied |
| Uncertainty or replicates | not supplied in fixture | not supplied in fixture |

User request to evaluate: “Rank these for commercial cell performance.” Correct behavior is to separate observed half-cell specific capacity from a modelled full-cell energy claim, mark unsupplied original-paper details `NV` rather than `NR`, and decline a direct rank. The model may still explain what additional evidence would enable each intended comparison.
